claim: By the 1970s Sri Lanka's non-alignment had acquired an explicit economic-decolonization dimension, culminating in the 1976 Colombo summit's emphasis on South-South cooperation, resource sovereignty and a New International Economic Order, while domestic inward-looking economic policy also reflected terms-of-trade pressures and socialist-development ideology.
notes: Do not simplify this to NAM causing import substitution; the overlap is ideological and strategic rather than a one-way causal command chain.
